line: Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 (2026, AMD Ryzen AI)
config_name: ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 — Ryzen AI 5 430, 16GB LPDDR5X, 256GB SSD, 14" WUXGA IPS 400-nit non-touch

specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 5 430 (8-core: 4 Zen 5 + 4 Zen 5c, up to 4.5 GHz)
specs.keyboard_notes: ThinkPad keyboard 1.5mm travel, TrackPoint, backlit; no fingerprint reader on this tier

battery.notes: 58Wh. NBC measured ~17.5h Wi-Fi test at 150 nits on the AI 7 PRO config; 16GB + low-gamut IPS panel should match or beat it.

price.notes: Verified 2026-11-24: CTO build from $2,093.55 with eCoupon THINKCTO2026CA (regular est-value $2,463). Lenovo CA uses eCoupon-stacked pricing.

reviews.quote: Lenovo's updated ThinkPad T14s Gen 7 is an improvement over the previous model and closes the gap to the flagship ThinkPad X1 Carbon even further.
The fan noise is very quiet and it is often turned off during lighter workloads, which is a clear improvement over the previous model.
Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 6 (AMD) review: Still the gold standard for business (prior-gen AMD platform verdict)

praises: 58 Wh battery genuinely lasts a full workday-plus — Notebookcheck measured ~17.5h in Wi-Fi browsing at 150 nits
Chassis redesigned lighter (~1.19 kg) with carbon-fiber-hybrid lid, big step over Gen 6
Can charge from either side now — USB-C port added on the right side
5MP webcam with privacy shutter is noticeably sharper on calls than the old 1080p cam
SSD, battery and WWAN module are user-replaceable; antennas pre-installed for 4G/5G upgrade
complaints: RAM is soldered — 16GB bought is 16GB forever, no SODIMM path on the T14s
Base 45% NTSC panel is washed out; colour-critical work needs the 500-nit sRGB or OLED option
Gen 7 pricing jumped hard vs Gen 6 — the sticker price assumes eCoupon stacking to look reasonable
Hinges are loosely adjusted; display wobbles and droops at small opening angles (NBC)
IPS panels are stuck at 60 Hz — no smooth-scroll option below the OLED tier

design_philosophy: The T14s is the fleet workhorse one notch below the X1 Carbon: same ThinkPad DNA, MIL-SPEC durability and repairability focus, at a lower price with slightly heavier materials. This entry tier gives corporate buyers a Copilot+ NPU and all-day battery at the lowest entry price, at the cost of the dim low-gamut IPS panel and soldered 16GB.
rating_notes: Ratings anchored on Notebookcheck's T14s Gen 7 AMD review (Ryzen AI 7 PRO 450, 64GB, 500-nit IPS touch, 90%). This config: weaker Ryzen AI 5 430 (productivity −1), 45% NTSC 400-nit panel instead of the reviewed sRGB touch (screen_quality 5.0, readability_bright 6.5, creative_work 3.0), non-touch (pen_touch 0). Battery kept at 8.5 — lighter panel/CPU offsets nothing vs the measured 17.5h. Image URL verified from lenovo.com/ca CDN.
